translationRepairs: He was soon promoted to left chief clerk of the Secretariat.
He was soon promoted to left chief clerk to the minister of education.

s0019 尋遷司徒左長史 names the office under 司徒 (minister of education / one of the Three Dukes), not the Secretariat (中書); “left chief clerk of the Secretariat” is a mistranslation, and the proposed replacement matches the Chinese.
When Emperor Xuan was regent he made Zhi left chief clerk of the Secretariat, retaining his general's title.
When Emperor Xuan was regent he made Zhi left chief clerk to the minister of education, retaining his general's title.

s0122 以為司徒左長史 again has 司徒, not 中書; “left chief clerk of the Secretariat” is wrong, and “left chief clerk to the minister of education” correctly renders the office while keeping the regency and general-title clauses intact.
He then sent Zai's clansman Hui bearing a letter to explain to Zai the reason for executing Wang Sengbian, and also presented an edict of Emperor Jing of Liang, edict ordering Zai to disarm.
He then sent Zai's clansman Hui bearing a letter to explain to Zai the reason for executing Wang Sengbian, and also presented an edict of Emperor Jing of Liang ordering Zai to disarm.

s0147 并奉梁敬帝敕，敕載解兵 is one edict that orders Zai to disarm; the literal’s bare second “edict” is broken English, and dropping the redundant noun keeps the letter, Jing’s edict, and the disarm order without adding or omitting content.
His grandfather Ai was Liang general who assists the state.
His grandfather Ai was Liang's General Who Assists the State.

s0162 梁輔國將軍 is the formal title 輔國將軍 under Liang; “Liang general who assists the state” reads as a bare common noun and is ungrammatical, while “Liang's General Who Assists the State” correctly titles the office.
During Taijian he died in office and was posthumously presented as inspector of Ming, Huo, and Luo provinces.
During Taijian he died in office and was posthumously made inspector of Ming, Huo, and Luo provinces.
s0173 贈明、霍、羅三州刺史 uses 贈 for posthumous conferral of office; “presented as” misstates that sense, and “posthumously made” matches the appointment meaning already used in the idiomatic field.
